sanskrit: yā te prajāpihitā parābhūd yonir vā mugdhā nihitā piśācaiḥ | āsnānaṃ vā yad abhitaṣṭhātha ghoraṃ sarvaṃ tat te brahmaṇā sūdayāmi ||
english: Whatever offspring-bearing capacity of yours has been obstructed and undone, or whose womb has been befouled and beset by piśācas; or whatever dreadful impurity has taken hold at the bathing-place — all that I purify for you by means of sacred brahman-power.

sanskrit: yady asyāḥ prajā varuṇena guṣpitā durṇāmāno vā ṛtviyam asyā rihanti | dveṣāt sāpatnād yadi cakrur asyā ayaṃ tā nāṣṭrā apa hantv agniḥ ||
english: If the offspring of this woman have been throttled by Varuṇa, or if ill-named beings lick away her fertile season; if from hatred of a co-wife they have wrought this upon her — may this fire, the destroyer of harmful things, strike those evils away.

sanskrit: asyā striyā yadi lakṣmīr aputryā garbho vāsyā yātudhānaiḥ parābhṛtaḥ | duḥsvapnyaṃ vā yat svapatī dadarśa- -indrāgnī tat kṛṇutāṃ bhadrayā punaḥ ||
english: If this woman's mark of fortune brings childlessness, or if her embryo has been carried off by yātudhānas; or if a bad dream has been seen while she slept — may Indra and Agni restore all that with auspiciousness once more.

sanskrit: devainasād yadi putraṃ na vindase manuṣyāṇāṃ vā tvā śapatho rarādha | pitṛbhir vā te yadi sūtaḥ pariṣṭhita idaṃ taṃ niṣ kṛṇmo janayāsi putram ||
english: If through a sin against the gods you do not obtain a son, or if a curse from men has afflicted you; or if your birth has been hemmed in by the Fathers — this we now undo entirely, so that you shall bring forth a son.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro janmanā jātavedāḥ prajāpatiḥ siñcatu reto asyām | bādhatāṃ dveṣo nirṛtiṃ parācaiḥ putriṇīm imāṃ prasvaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas who is so from birth, Prajāpati, pour seed into her. Let him drive away hatred and Nirṛti to the far distance; may he make this woman one who bears sons and gives birth with ease.

sanskrit: iha prajām agnir asyai dadhātv ādityebhir vasubhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ | viśve devā havam ā yantu ma imaṃ putro asyā jāyatāṃ vīryāvān ||
english: May Agni here grant progeny to this woman, united with the Ādityas and the Vasus. Let all the gods come to my invocation — may her son be born, endowed with heroic vigor.

sanskrit: yena devy aditir garbham ādadhe yena prajā asṛjata prajāpatiḥ | tenāham asyai haviṣā juhomi yathā pumāṃsaṃ janayāti putram ||
english: By that same means whereby divine Aditi received the embryo, whereby Prajāpati sent forth offspring — by that same power I offer oblation for her with this havir, so that she may bring forth a male child, a son.

sanskrit: vanve te putraṃ pari devatābhyo anu manyantāṃ marutaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ | garbhas tvā daśamāsyaḥ pra viśatu kumāraṃ jātaṃ pipṛtām upasthe ||
english: I beg a son for you from the deities; may the Maruts, born of Pṛśni, consent. May the ten-month embryo enter you; when the boy is born, may he be nurtured at your lap.

sanskrit: keśy agniṃ keśī viṣaṃ keśī bibharti rodasī | keśī viśvaṃ svar dṛśe keśīdaṃ jyotir ucyate ||
english: The Long-haired one bears fire; the Long-haired one bears poison; the Long-haired one sustains the two worlds. The Long-haired one is all that is, to behold the sun — the Long-haired one is called this very light.

sanskrit: munayo vātaraśanāḥ piśaṅgā vasate malāḥ | vātasyānu dhrājiṃ yanti yad devāso ayukṣata ||
english: The munis girt by wind, tawny-hued, clad in soiled garments — they follow along the rushing course of the wind, there where the gods have yoked themselves.

sanskrit: unmaditā mauneyena vātām̐ ā tasthimā vayam | śarīred asmākaṃ yūyaṃ martāso abhi paśyatha ||
english: Intoxicated by the state of mauneya — the silent wisdom — we have mounted the winds. You mortals look only upon our bodies.

sanskrit: antarikṣeṇa patati svar bhūtāvacākaśat | munir devasya-devasya saukṛtyāya sakhā hitaḥ ||
english: Through the mid-air he flies, gazing down upon all living beings below as upon the sun. The muni, friend set in place for the welfare of every single god.

sanskrit: indrasyāśvo vāyoḥ sakhā- -atho deveṣito muniḥ | ubhā samudrāv ā kṣayati sadyaḥ pūrvam utāparam ||
english: The steed of Indra, the companion of Vāyu — and moreover the muni impelled by the gods: he dwells in both oceans at once, in a single instant, both the eastern and the western.

sanskrit: gandharvāṇām apsarasāṃ devānāṃ caraṇe caran | muniḥ ketasya saṃvidvān sakhā svādur madintamaḥ ||
english: Wandering in the pathway of the Gandharvas, the Apsarases, and the gods, the muni, knowing the intention of the wise, is a sweet and supremely ecstatic companion.

sanskrit: vāyur asmā upāmanthat pinaṣṭi smā kunaṃnamā | munir viṣasya pātreṇa yad rudreṇāpibat saha ||
english: Vāyu churned for him; Kunaṃnamā — the bent one — ground the herbs. The muni, together with Rudra, drank from the cup of poison.

sanskrit: saṃyukte dyāvāpṛthivī tiṣṭhantī avicartye | keśenaikasya devasya vy aṣṭabhnāc chacīpatiḥ ||
english: Heaven and Earth standing joined together, immovable and inseparable — by the hair of a single god did the lord of Śacī prop them apart.

sanskrit: na tam aṃho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyam | sajoṣaso yam aryamā mitro nayanti varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: No affliction, no distress has reached that mortal, O gods, whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa — of one accord — lead safely past the haters.

sanskrit: tad dhi vayaṃ vṛṇīmahe varuṇa mitrāryaman | yan no nir aṃhaso yūyaṃ pātha nethā ca martyam ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: For this very boon we choose you, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman: that you protect us free from anguish and guide the mortal past the haters.

sanskrit: te nūnaṃ no yūyam ūtaye varuṇa (…) | nayiṣṭhā no neṣiṇa stha parṣiṣṭāḥ parṣiṇo ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: So now, you — for our aid, O Varuṇa [Mitra, Aryaman] — you are the surest guides, you are leaders; you who have carried across shall carry us across, past the haters.

sanskrit: śunam asmabhyam ūtaye varuṇa mitrāryaman | śarma yacchātha sapratha ādityāso yad īmahe ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: For auspicious aid to us, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — O Ādityas, grant us broad shelter, for which we beseech you, past the haters.

sanskrit: ādityāso ati sridho varuṇo mitro aryamā | rudraṃ marudbhir ugraṃ huvema- -indram agniṃ svastaye ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: The Ādityas — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — overcome those who would crush us. We invoke fierce Rudra along with the Maruts, Indra and Agni, for well-being, past the haters.

sanskrit: netāra ū ṣu ṇas tiro varuṇo mitro aryamā | ati viśvāni duritā rājānaś carṣaṇīnām ati dviṣaḥ ||
english: Do indeed guide us across, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — kings over all peoples — beyond all distresses, past the haters.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ viśvaṃ pari pātha varuṇa mitrāryaman | yuṣmākaṃ śarmaṇi priyā syāma supraṇītayo 'ti dviṣaḥ ||
english: You protect everything, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman. May we be beloved in your shelter, well-led by you, past the haters.

sanskrit: yathā ha tyad vasavo gauryaṃ cit padi ṣitām amuñcatā yajatrāḥ | evo ṣv asman muñcatā vy aṃhaḥ pra tāry agne prataraṃ na āyuḥ ||
english: Just as, O Vasus, O adorable ones, you released even the Gaurī cow that was bound at the foot — so do release us from anguish; O Agni, extend our life yet further forward.
